title: Toad in the Hole
subtitle: Pork sausages baked in a crisp Yorkshire pudding batter
excerpt: Pork sausages nestled in a crisp, puffed Yorkshire pudding batter and baked in a very hot oven until golden all over. Served with onion gravy and mashed potato. One of Britain's great comfort dishes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Toad in the hole has been a British favourite since at least the 18th century, when it was made with any available meat. By the Victorian era, pork sausages had become standard. The dish uses the same batter as Yorkshire pudding. The critical technique is identical: the fat must be smoking hot before the cold batter goes in, and the oven door must not be opened during baking. The sausages brown on the outside while the batter rises around them.

recipeTools.notes: A high-sided roasting tin, roughly 30 x 20 cm.

content.text: Rest the batter for at least 30 minutes before using: this gives a lighter, more even rise. The fat in the tin must be smoking hot when the batter goes in. This is what creates the dramatic rise and crisp edges. Do not open the oven door for the first 20 minutes of baking or the batter will collapse.
Make the batter: whisk the flour, eggs, milk, salt, and pepper together until smooth. Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Pour the oil into the roasting tin and add the sausages. Roast for 15 minutes until the sausages are lightly browned and the fat is smoking hot.

Working quickly, pour the batter into the hot tin around the sausages. Return to the oven immediately. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the batter is puffed, golden, and crisp. Do not open the oven for the first 20 minutes. Serve immediately.
